content_preview.title: Researcher Shows Low-Privilege Database Accounts Can Reach Code Execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle and ClickHouse
content_preview.summary: A Depthfirst researcher published proofs of concept turning memory-corruption bugs into code execution from low-privilege accounts on four database engines; vendors have shipped fixes.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A security researcher has published proof-of-concept exploits showing that database accounts without permission to read a single application table can still run code on the database server itself, by reaching memory-corruption bugs buried in the engine code that processes ordinary SQL, according to [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/researcher-demonstrates-database-rce.html). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece using the standard Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know/Implications frame, with a per-engine breakdown (PostgreSQL/MySQL/Oracle Database/ClickHouse) in bolded sub-headers. Neutral, attributive tone throughout -- every claim is hedged with 'according to', 'the outlet reported', or 'the researcher says'. No AI self-reference, no sensationalism. Word count 846 is within the 400-1200 News range. Title is 117 characters, within the 150-character limit. The writer reports it used zero quoted text and instead paraphrased with attribution to eliminate quote-fidelity risk; verified true by grepping the raw submission JSON for any straight or curly double-quote character inside body_markdown -- zero matches found anywhere in the body.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both snapshots in sources/2026-11/researcher-shows-low-privilege-database-accounts-can-reach-code-execution-on-postgresql-mysql-oracle-and-clickhouse/ were read after re-hashing the decompressed content and confirming it matches manifest.json exactly: source-0.html.gz (thehackernews.com, sha256 c56e987f...) and source-1.html.gz (postgresql.org CVE-2026-116331 advisory, sha256 323ede0a...). suspicious_patterns is null for both entries in manifest.json -- no prompt-injection content found in either snapshot. source-1 (postgresql.org) independently confirms every PostgreSQL-specific detail in the article verbatim: CVE-2026-116331, 'Type confusion in PostgreSQL min/max aggregate optimization... via a user-defined aggregate whose SORTOP option causes the planner to treat the aggregate's input and result as the same type when they differ', affected versions before 18.7/17.12/16.16/15.20/14.25, fix published 2026-11-12 for all five branches, and CVSS 3.0 score 8.8. source-0 (The Hacker News, by Swati Khandelwal, dated Nov 19, 2026, with a Nov 20, 2026 correction notice already incorporated into the live text) confirms: the researcher's identity ('The work is by Zheng Yu, a researcher at Depthfirst'); the four-engine/five-flaw PostgreSQL+MySQL+ClickHouse+Oracle(no-login) scope; the 'None has been seen in a real attack' line; the TEMPORARY-privilege/temporary-table mechanism description; the MySQL CVE-2026-101786 details (Server/Cluster 26.7.0-26.7.1, Oracle's October advisory rating it 'high privileges' versus the researcher's narrower temp-table-only account); the Oracle Database no-login chain (Oracle Text CVE-2026-114819 rated 9.9 patched in the November update, ORDS GraphQL flaw CVE-2026-91609 patched in the October update, neither rated exploitable alone without login per Oracle); the ClickHouse integer-overflow via format_binary_max_string_size=0, reproduced on 26.7.5.10, no CVE assigned, reported via ClickHouse's bug bounty, fixed in early September with the open-source fix in 26.9+ and backported to 26.8.3.41/26.7.7.30/26.6.5.55/26.3.32.8; and the closing mitigation guidance (review account capabilities, strip TEMPORARY/temp-table rights, note this does not close the Oracle no-account path). Source independence: this is a News article (no minimum independent-source-count requirement, unlike Analysis); both sources are independent of the researcher and the vendors (The Hacker News is independent trade press, PostgreSQL.org is the vendor's own advisory used only to corroborate the PostgreSQL-specific CVE/version/CVSS data, which is appropriate first-party use for that narrow purpose). Anthropic disclosure: not required - the story's subject is database-engine vulnerability research; Anthropic, Claude, or an Anthropic-owned product is never mentioned in the article body.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Core technical claim verified true against raw source text: Zheng Yu of Depthfirst published PoCs reaching code execution from low-privilege accounts on PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus a separate no-login Oracle Database chain -- this is stated almost verbatim in the Hacker News snapshot ('The exploits... are the researcher's proofs of concept against PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus a separate Oracle chain that needs no login'). The 'none observed in a real attack' claim is verified true against the same snapshot ('None has been seen in a real attack... the research reports no sign that any of them has been used in an attack'). The writer separately reported excluding a WebFetch hallucination -- a fabricated quote-formatted sentence and invented Oracle/ORDS version ranges -- from an earlier research pass; neither appears anywhere in the final submission text: no quote marks exist in body_markdown (confirmed above), and the article never states specific Oracle Text or ORDS version ranges (it only gives CVE IDs and patch months), so the invented ranges were not carried through. However, in avoiding the invented ranges the writer introduced a new, independent error: the 'What We Don't Know' section states 'The Hacker News's reporting does not specify the exact affected version ranges for the Oracle Database and Oracle REST Data Services flaws beyond noting when each was patched.' This is false. The Hacker News snapshot contains an explicit summary table with exact version ranges for both: 'Oracle Database (Oracle Text) | CVE-2026-114819 | 19.3-19.32, 21.3-21.24, 23.4.0-23.26.3 | Fixed November 17' and 'Oracle REST Data Services | CVE-2026-91609 | 24.2.0 to 26.2.1 | Fixed October 20'. This is a wrong absence claim in a subordinate paragraph (not the headline, summary, or lead) -- the article's core claims about the vulnerabilities, the researcher, the mechanism, and the 'none observed in the wild' line are all independently verified accurate. Handled as an APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS correction rather than a REJECT. All other specifics (CVE IDs, CVSS scores, affected version numbers for PostgreSQL and MySQL, ClickHouse build numbers, patch dates/months) were checked individually against the raw snapshots and match exactly.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; every claim is attributed to the outlet, the researcher, or the vendor advisory rather than stated as the Herald's own assertion. No loaded language, no editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for 'Zheng Yu', 'Depthfirst', and all four CVE IDs -- no prior Herald coverage of this story. One tangential prior piece exists (src/content/articles/2026-05/16-depthfirsts-ai-scanner-surfaces-nginx-rift-...) about a different Depthfirst product (an AI vulnerability scanner finding an nginx bug) and is unrelated to this researcher's manual PoC work; not a duplicate.
concerns: The 'What We Don't Know' section incorrectly states that The Hacker News's reporting does not specify exact affected version ranges for the Oracle Database (Oracle Text) and Oracle REST Data Services flaws; the source's own summary table does specify them (19.3-19.32, 21.3-21.24, 23.4.0-23.26.3 for CVE-2026-114819; 24.2.0 to 26.2.1 for CVE-2026-91609). This is a subordinate claim, not in the headline/summary/lead, so it is addressed with a corrections record rather than a rejection.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced News article covering real research across four major database engines, with the central technical claims (researcher identity, four-engine/five-flaw scope, the no-login Oracle chain, and the 'none observed in the wild' line) independently verified against raw source text. The writer's quote-avoidance and hallucination-exclusion efforts both checked out, but a new, unrelated absence-claim error appeared in the What We Don't Know section (Oracle/ORDS version ranges are in fact specified by the cited source), which is being corrected publicly rather than silently fixed. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate security research spanning four widely deployed database engines, of clear interest to a defined DBA/security-engineering audience, but tempered by the fact that fixes already shipped and no in-the-wild exploitation was found.
